docs_verified.api: semver.compare(v1, v2): returns 0 when v1 == v2, 1 when v1 is greater, -1 when v2 is greater; imported as the package's default CommonJS export (require('semver') / import semver from 'semver').
docs_verified.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/npm/node-semver/main/README.md (fetched live; context7 has no /npm/node-semver entry for the JS package, only same-named libraries in other languages, so the official README was used per security-hygiene.verify-current-docs' fallback).

docs_verified.api: pnpm add: -e, --save-exact installs the exact resolved version instead of a semver range.
docs_verified.source: mise exec -- pnpm help add (pnpm 11.18.0, pinned by this repository's mise.toml).

dependencies.name: semver
dependencies.evidence: pnpm view semver: 119 published versions, zero runtime dependencies, latest 7.8.5 published 2 months ago by the npm org's release automation; four active maintainers (saquibkhan, npm-cli-ops, reggi, owlstronaut). It is node-semver, "the semver parser for node (the one npm itself uses)". GitHub (npm/node-semver): 557 commits, 5.5k stars, 598 forks, 42 open issues against an active 17-PR queue, CI workflows and a security policy in place — an actively maintained, widely-depended-on core ecosystem package.

self_review: Diff is minimal and complete: one exact-pinned devDependency (semver 7.8.5), one helper module, one test file; no stray edits, no TODOs.
compareVersions(a, b) is documented with a JSDoc block matching this repository's tests/ helper convention (tests/scratch-dir.mjs); the exported symbol is the only one in the file.

Placement: the helper lives in tests/, not template/tools/lib/, because template/ carries the standing invariant houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins (Node built-ins only, no dependency) and this repository's devDependencies are documented to serve its tests and commit hook only (houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins body) - adding an npm-dependent helper to the shipped kit payload would have broken every project that installs it.

Test asserts real behavior, not just that a call succeeds: the numeric-vs-lexical ordering case (1.2.3 sorts before 1.10.0) would fail under a naive string compare, so it verifies compareVersions actually delegates to semantic comparison rather than trivially passing.
No focused tests (no .only), no version numbers hand-typed in package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml (both came from pnpm add --save-exact --save-dev).

Coverage gate is unaffected: the vitest config's coverage.include list is a fixed set of existing files and does not include tests/*.mjs helpers, matching how tests/scratch-dir.mjs is already excluded.
concerns: The helper is not wired into any existing test or CLI; the brief asked only for a helper module plus a failing-test-first cycle, and I kept it standalone per YAGNI rather than inventing an integration point (e.g. bin/houserules.mjs's version-drift line) beyond what was asked.
